quiz_questions.question: According to ICMR-NIN guidelines (National Nutrition Week 2026), what is the recommended daily dietary protein intake for an average sedentary Indian adult?
options: 0.83 g per kg of ideal body weight
2.5 g per kg of ideal body weight
0.2 g per kg of ideal body weight
quiz_questions.explanation: ICMR-NIN (National Institute of Nutrition) recommends approximately 0.83g of high-quality protein per kg of body weight for a sedentary adult (approx. 54g for a 65kg adult) to prevent sarcopenia and maintain immune defense.

quiz_questions.question: Which of the following budget-friendly indigenous Indian foods provides the highest amount of plant-based protein per 100g dry weight?
options: Soya Chunks / Defatted Soy Flour (approx 52g protein)
quiz_questions.explanation: Defatted Soya Chunks contain an astounding ~52g protein per 100g at a cost of merely ₹15-20 per 100g, making it the most cost-effective protein source in the Indian market!

quiz_questions.question: What is the traditional 'Cereal-Pulse Complementarity' principle in Indian Thalis (e.g., Dal-Chawal or Roti-Dal)?
options: It makes the food taste sweet without sugar
Cereals are deficient in Lysine but rich in Methionine, while Pulses are rich in Lysine but deficient in Methionine; combining them creates a complete amino acid profile!
It reduces the cooking time of lentils by half
It eliminates all carbohydrates from the diet
quiz_questions.explanation: Traditional Indian combinations like Dal-Roti, Khichdi, or Idli-Sambar pair cereals (rich in methionine) with legumes/pulses (rich in lysine) to provide a complete essential amino acid profile equivalent to animal proteins!
